questions.explanation: The text says change comes from 'small shifts in everyday speech' and academies have had 'only limited success'.
questions.passage: The prevailing view among linguists is that languages change gradually, driven less by deliberate decisions than by countless small shifts in everyday speech. Attempts by academies to fix a language in place have therefore met with only limited success; usage, in the end, tends to outrun rule.

items.q: What drives language change, according to most linguists?
How successful have academies been at fixing language?

questions.passage: Reviewers were quick to dismiss the exhibition as derivative, yet its curator remained unruffled.
